subject: SLO deep-dive & PoC alignment — Synergia (post-call recap)
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Harper <alex.harper@synergia.ai>, Priya Sethi <priya@synergia.ai>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: SLO deep-dive & PoC alignment — Synergia (post-call recap)

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks again for the time today. Quick written recap so we have a single source of truth and clear next steps. I captured both the customer pain + measurable acceptance criteria we discussed, and a suggested PoC scope & topology options.

Summary of pain / goals (what we heard)
- Real-time claims categorization pipeline: 200–400 QPS peak expected for Phase 1, burst to ~1,000 QPS during monthly ingest windows.
- Per-interaction latency target (p95) at or under 150ms for short responses (<=256 tokens); p99 target <= 350ms.
- Deterministic tail behavior is more important than lowest median — they need predictable SLA for downstream routing.
- On-prem data residency for PHI in Year 2; Phase 1 can run in managed VPC with customer KMS.

Model & workload constraints
- Primary model is a fine-tuned 7B text classification/generation variant (few-shot prompts, ~128 tokens output).
- KV cache likely to benefit self-consistent session workloads (same patient dialogue sequences).
- Expect 60–70% of requests to be short classification queries (fast-path).~30% will be longer generation where latency budget can be relaxed.

Suggested PoC acceptance criteria (agreed during call)
- Demonstrate sustained 200 QPS for 1 hour with p95 <= 150ms and no production errors > 0.1%.
- End-to-end integration with their API gateway + auth (mutual TLS or OIDC) and encrypted logging to S3 in a separate account.
- Basic regression check on a 100-case prompt suite (we'll run evals and report token cost delta).

Topology options we reviewed
1) Hosted PoC (fastest): Redwood hosted with dedicated pool + VPC peering — recommended for speed to results.
2) Dedicated reserved capacity: predictable throughput; recommended if Synergia wants consistent latency at scale and commitment.
3) Private on-prem (Year 2): customer-managed nodes with Redwood control plane — for PHI residency.

Immediate asks from our side
- Can you share one representative sample dataset (anonymized) and the monthly ingest cadence? (Priya)
- Procurement timeline & required contract terms (Alex) — you mentioned a November roll target for production.

Attachments: I attached a short PoC MOP (redwood-synergia-poc-mop.pdf) and a latency/throughput estimate workbook. Also linking the shared PoC folder below.

Proposed next steps
- We will produce a mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones and a 2-week PoC scope. Action owner: Connor (deliver Monday 2026-07-19).
- Technical kickoff session with infra (1h): propose Wed 2026-07-21 09:30 PT. Action owner: Mina to lead the technical runbook review.
- Procurement: Alex to share any standard SLA/contract must-haves; Connor to coordinate with Legal.

If I've missed anything or you want this reshaped into a one-pager, say the word and I'll convert it.

Thanks — Connor
Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0137

Attachments referenced: redwood-synergia-poc-mop.pdf, latency-throughput-estimates.xlsx

From: Alex Harper <alex.harper@synergia.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Sethi <priya@synergia.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 18:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLO deep-dive & PoC alignment — Synergia (post-call recap)

Connor — this is great, thanks for the clear write-up. A few clarifications from our side:
- We can share an anonymized subset of records (approx. 5k messages) by Friday; that should be sufficient for initial throughput tuning.
- Procurement: our legal team needs to review data processing terms around PHI — target procurement window is late Sep / early Oct; production by Nov is still our ideal but flexible.
- Security: I attached our security questionnaire (synergia-security-q.pdf). Can you confirm Redwood’s SOC2 scope and any on-prem compliance options?

We’re aligned on the acceptance criteria you listed. For the PoC, we prefer Redwood to run the hosted PoC first so we can validate SLOs before committing to Dedicated.

Also: one nit — for the p99 target you suggested 350ms; given our internal routing, if we can keep p99 <= 500ms for the generation paths that’s acceptable as long as the classification fast-path meets 150ms.

I’ll confirm availability for the proposed technical kickoff tomorrow.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Harper
Head of ML Platforms | Synergia Solutions

Attachment: synergia-security-q.pdf

- p95 <= 150ms for classification fast-path; p99 for generation paths target <= 500ms for PoC (note: we will propose optimizations — quantization, batching controls, and routing fallbacks — if we need to tighten tails).
- Tech kickoff: Wed 2026-07-21 09:30 PT is confirmed for Mina and Karthik.

Action items updated:
- Connor: deliver MAP + test plan by Mon 2026-07-19 (includes test dataset instructions & SLI checks).

- Karthik: draft suggested model variants / quantization options for meeting p95 SLOs (deliver by 2026-07-20).

I’ll upload the MAP draft to the drive and ping you later today.

Thanks — Connor

Subject: Internal: Synergia PoC prep & ask list

Quick internal note following the external thread — copying context and a concise set of asks so Mina/Karthik have everything in one place.

TL;DR (what Synergia needs)
- Hosted PoC first: demonstrate sustained 200 QPS with p95 <= 150ms (classification). Allowable p99 for generation <= 500ms during PoC.
- Sample dataset (5k anonymized rows) and security questionnaire incoming.
- Procurement window likely Sept; curtail expectations for Dedicated commit until PoC results.

Mina — please prepare two deliverables by Tue 2026-07-20:
1) Capacity estimate: hosted PoC sizing (GPU types, pool size, expected token cost) and a Dedicated baseline (monthly commit estimate). Use the attached workbook as starting point.
2) Ops runbook stub: VPC peering, mutual TLS setup, and logging configs we’ll propose.

Karthik — can you: 
- Outline 2 model variants we should test (7B FP16 baseline; 7B int8 quantized fast-path) and expected latency deltas.
- Call out any kernel/runtime worries for the 128-token generation path at 1k burst QPS.

I’ll finalize the MAP draft and assign tasks in HubSpot after we get Alex’s dataset; I’ll also attach the redwood-synergia-poc-mop.pdf to the deal.

Connor
